narrativeReportMd:
# ResearchStudy R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking changes found. R6 keeps the same canonical resource identity, but remodels many local elements. Existing R4 instances commonly need transformation before R6 validation.

## Scope
Compared local R4 and R6 core StructureDefinitions and related local terminology. Excluded inherited base-resource changes and SearchParameters.

## Main migration themes
The major themes are: `status` changed meaning and required value set; broad R4 fields were split into more explicit R6 structures; `focus` changed to CodeableReference; enrollment, parties, relationships, and arms were remodeled; and R6 adds optional scientific/result/progress content that R4 cannot represent natively.

## Highest-impact findings
Highest-impact findings are `status`, `focus`, `relatedArtifact`, `enrollment`/`recruitment`, party/contact modeling, and `arm`/`comparisonGroup`.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed for lifecycle status mapping, broad category classification, enrollment Group roles, RelatedArtifact target choice, sponsor/contact role mapping, and R6-only outcome/progress/result backports.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several path breaks could have been softened by deprecated aliases. The R6 design usually improves expressivity, but many changes are not wire-compatible with R4 JSON.

## Follow-up analysis
Official ConceptMaps, narrative diffs, and terminology expansions would improve code-level migration guidance.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `ResearchStudy` has high-impact local breaking changes despite stable artifact identity. Top concerns are the `status` semantic/binding change, major element remodeling (`focus`, recruitment, parties, relationships, comparison groups), and R6-only content that cannot be represented in R4 without extensions. Main uncertainty is official terminology/ConceptMap guidance.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Treat migration as a ResearchStudy-specific transform. Some changes are direct renames, but many require semantic classification: split lifecycle from publication status, classify R4 categories, wrap focus as CodeableReference, map enrollment Groups into recruitment roles, role-code parties, and preserve R6-only progress/outcome/result content for R4 clients.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural breaks because both StructureDefinitions were present and compared directly. Confidence is medium for exact semantic/code mappings where official diffs, narrative rationale, ConceptMaps, or external terminology expansions were absent.

findings.title: ResearchStudy.status changed from study lifecycle status to publication status

oldState.summary: R4 `status` is required, modifier, summary, and bound required to research-study-status; it means the current state of the study.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `status` is required, modifier, summary, and bound required to research-study-status; it means the current state of the study.

binding.description: Codes that convey the current status of the research study.

semanticText.definition: The current state of the study.

newState.summary: R6 `status` is still required, modifier, and summary, but is bound required to publication-status and means the publication state of the resource.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `status` is still required, modifier, and summary, but is bound required to publication-status and means the publication state of the resource.

binding.description: Codes that convey the current publication status of the research study resource.

semanticText.definition: The publication state of the resource (not of the study).

facts.newValue: publication state of the ResearchStudy resource

facts.field: R4 study status codes not in R6 publication-status

facts.note: Both code systems have an `active` code, but R4 active means opened for accrual while R6 active means ready for normal resource use.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation break for most R4 instances and a semantic break for the path that survived. R4 codes such as `completed` or `approved` fail the R6 required binding. The overlapping literal `active` can validate while changing meaning.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate publication status of the artifact record from operational study progress.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep lifecycle `status` and add a separate publication-status element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal is reasonable: distinguish the publication state of the ResearchStudy record from the operational progress of the study. However, repurposing a required modifier path is highly disruptive because many R4 lifecycle codes fail validation and overlapping literals such as `active` change meaning. A less-breaking design exists, but it would not cleanly provide a mandatory, uniform publication-status slot at the existing `status` path, so the break is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained R4 `status` for study lifecycle and added a new publication-status element while using `progressStatus` for detailed study progress. That would preserve old R4 status codes and avoid same-path semantic drift. The tradeoff is material: if the new publication-status element were optional or profile-enforced, base R6 would not guarantee a computable publication status for every ResearchStudy; if it were mandatory, old R4 instances would still need new data. Maintaining two status-like fields also creates validation and interoperability burden.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 data but leaves two status concepts and weakens same-path publication-status consistency.

evidence.detail: R4 required binding is research-study-status|4.0.1.
R6 required binding is publication-status|6.0.0-ballot4.
The local R4 code system includes completed, approved, closed-to-accrual, withdrawn, and other study lifecycle codes.
The local R6 publication-status code system contains draft, active, retired, and unknown.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments isolate the status migration; a production transform must decide the publication status independently.

findings.narrativeMd: `status` is the most important local breaking change. It keeps the same path and cardinality, so parsers may not fail early when the code happens to overlap, but business meaning changes from study state to publication state.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances using any non-`active` R4 research-study-status code become invalid in R6. R6 instances using `draft`, `retired`, or `unknown` cannot be represented in R4 `status` without an extension or lossy lifecycle mapping.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not copy `status` mechanically. Determine R6 publication status separately and map the old study lifecycle value to `progressStatus.state` when possible; test all R4 status codes, especially the ambiguous `active` case.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible alias or new publication-status element could have avoided this break. R6 instead chose a cleaner common publication-status pattern.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: No official ConceptMap was available for lifecycle-to-publication status mapping.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `ResearchStudy.status` is a required modifier carrying the study lifecycle state, while R6 keeps the same required modifier path but changes it to publication status of the resource. That creates both validator failures for most R4 lifecycle codes and a same-code semantic trap for `active`. Because this path is mandatory, modifier-marked, and central to study registry exchange, the break looks disproportionate even though ResearchStudy was only FMM 1 in R4.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition `ResearchStudy.status`: min 1, modifier, required binding to `research-study-status`, definition `The current state of the study`.
R6 StructureDefinition `ResearchStudy.status`: min 1, modifier, required binding to `publication-status`, definition `The publication state of the resource (not of the study)`.
R4 CodeSystem includes lifecycle codes such as `approved`, `completed`, `closed-to-accrual`, and `withdrawn`; R6 publication-status has only `draft`, `active`, `retired`, and `unknown`.
Local StructureDefinition mappings tie ResearchStudy fields to ClinicalTrials.gov and BRIDG; Vulcan RWD IG describes clinical research FHIR data used for EHR retrieval and regulatory submissions.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 1/trial-use softens the general stability expectation, but not enough for a required modifier path whose meaning changed from operational study lifecycle to publication state.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: most R4 status codes fail the R6 required binding; runtime/API/codegen risk also exists because the path survives while `active` changes meaning.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could have retained lifecycle `status` and added a separate publication-status element, possibly with profiles requiring it. The tradeoff is two status concepts and weaker base uniformity if the new element is optional, but it would avoid same-path semantic drift on a required modifier.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing High impact assessment is right, but the less-breaking alternative is more compelling than the prior `Partial/probably justified` framing because the retained modifier path creates semantic misinterpretation, not just migration work.

findings.title: primaryPurposeType was replaced by purposeType with wider cardinality and weaker binding

oldState.summary: R4 `primaryPurposeType` is 0..1 CodeableConcept, summary, with extensible research-study-prim-purp-type binding.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `primaryPurposeType` is 0..1 CodeableConcept, summary, with extensible research-study-prim-purp-type binding.

newState.summary: R6 `purposeType` is 0..* CodeableConcept, summary, with example terminology.hl7.org research-study-prim-purp-type binding.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `purposeType` is 0..* CodeableConcept, summary, with example terminology.hl7.org research-study-prim-purp-type binding.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Same definition family, same binding name, and same BRIDG mapping.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 JSON with `primaryPurposeType` is invalid in R6. R6 can also carry multiple purpose types, which R4's singular element cannot represent losslessly.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow multiple study purposes under a shorter name.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `primaryPurposeType` and broaden its cardinality/definition, or keep it as a deprecated alias.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing multiple study purposes is reasonable, but the evidence shows a close replacement with the same concept family and mappings. The serialization break comes mainly from the rename, not from the need for repeatability or weaker terminology binding. Because R6 could have preserved most R4 instances by tolerating the old name, the breaking design is probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking design would keep `primaryPurposeType` as the wire element, widen it to `0..*`, and clarify that the legacy name now represents study purpose types generally rather than exactly one primary purpose. Another option is to add `purposeType` while retaining `primaryPurposeType` as a deprecated alias. The alias option has some duplicate-representation risk, but simply broadening the old element would meet the core repeatability goal with only the moderate cost of a less ideal historical name.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Legacy wording is awkward for multiple purposes but has low long-term cost compared with a hard path rename.

evidence.detail: R4 element is 0..1 CodeableConcept with extensible binding.
R6 element is 0..* CodeableConcept with example binding.
R4 maps to StudyProtocolVersion.primaryPurposeTypeCode; R6 `purposeType` uses the same mapping.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 array form is required even when only one old value exists.

findings.narrativeMd: The apparent replacement is high-confidence: same concept, same primary-purpose terminology family, and same BRIDG mapping. The break is the element name and the changed cardinality/binding.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with `primaryPurposeType` has an unknown element in R6. An R6 instance with multiple `purposeType` values cannot be represented in R4 without choosing one or using extensions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `primaryPurposeType` to `purposeType` and wrap the old value in an array. For R6-to-R4, define a policy for multiple values and preserve extras as extensions if needed.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The same model goal could have been achieved by widening the existing element, so this is an avoidable serialization break.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `primaryPurposeType` was replaced by repeating R6 `purposeType` with the same concept family and BRIDG mapping. R4 instances with the old property will not validate as R6, and R6 instances with multiple purpose values cannot be reduced to R4 without policy. The change is real, but the old name and singular JSON shape do not preserve the R6 goal of multiple purposes very well.
keyEvidence: R4 `ResearchStudy.primaryPurposeType`: 0..1 CodeableConcept, extensible binding to `research-study-prim-purp-type`, BRIDG map `StudyProtocolVersion.primaryPurposeTypeCode`.
R6 `ResearchStudy.purposeType`: 0..* CodeableConcept, example binding to the terminology.hl7.org primary-purpose value set, same BRIDG mapping.
R6 no longer contains `ResearchStudy.primaryPurposeType`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1/trial-use materially softens the stability concern for this optional element; the break should be acknowledged but does not by itself imply broad production harm.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: the old path is absent in R6; R6-to-R4 loss occurs when more than one purpose is present.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Retaining `primaryPurposeType` unchanged while adding a new repeating purpose element would preserve R4 instances, but it creates duplicate purpose representations. Simply changing `primaryPurposeType` to 0..* would still change the FHIR JSON shape from object to array, so it is not fully compatibility-preserving.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing Medium impact is reasonable, but the existing `Yes` alternative overstates how easy preservation would be because the cardinality change itself changes wire shape unless a duplicate/deprecated element is retained.

findings.title: category was removed and split across studyDesign and classifier

oldState.summary: R4 `category` is 0..* CodeableConcept, summary, and broadly categorizes study type, blinding, randomization, safety/efficacy, and similar concepts.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `category` is 0..* CodeableConcept, summary, and broadly categorizes study type, blinding, randomization, safety/efficacy, and similar concepts.

newState.summary: R6 removes `category`; `studyDesign` covers study design characteristics with a preferred study-design binding, while `classifier` covers additional grouping/classification.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 removes `category`; `studyDesign` covers study design characteristics with a preferred study-design binding, while `classifier` covers additional grouping/classification.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Definitions and mappings support `studyDesign` as a partial replacement; `classifier` covers the remaining broad category use.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `category` is invalid in R6. The replacement is a semantic split, so automated migration must classify old category values instead of just renaming the path.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate study design characteristics from miscellaneous classifiers.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep deprecated broad `category` while adding `studyDesign` and `classifier`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating study design characteristics from other classifiers is a reasonable R6 modeling goal. A compatibility element could preserve R4 wire format, but the old `category` intentionally mixed design, blinding, randomization, safety/efficacy, and miscellaneous classifications. Keeping it in the base model would make the clearer R6 split incomplete and would require ongoing reconciliation rules, so the breaking split is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained `category` as deprecated while adding `studyDesign` and `classifier`. That would allow old R4 instances to validate and give senders time to migrate. The alternative is only partial because it leaves multiple ways to express the same classification and does not force ambiguous historical category values into the more precise R6 buckets.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old instances but perpetuates an ambiguous bucket and duplicate classification paths.

evidence.detail: R4 category is a broad 0..* CodeableConcept.
R6 studyDesign carries study design characteristics and shares the old mapping targets.
R6 classifier is an additional grouping mechanism and warns not to duplicate explicit semantics.

examples.examplesMd: The example assumes the category is study design; regulatory categories may belong in `classifier` instead.

findings.narrativeMd: `category` is not present in R6. `studyDesign` carries the same core definition and mappings, while `classifier` handles other grouping examples. The split improves precision but creates human-review migration cases.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Any R4 instance containing `category` is invalid as R6. R6 data in both `studyDesign` and `classifier` can be flattened to R4 only by losing which classification was design-related versus miscellaneous.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Classify each old category code/text into `studyDesign`, `classifier`, or another explicit R6 element. Use local code-system knowledge and preserve ambiguous values for review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A deprecated catch-all `category` would have been more compatible but less precise.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: R6 study-design terminology expansion was not available locally.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `category` was a broad repeating classifier for study type, blinding, randomization, safety/efficacy, and similar concepts. R6 splits that space across `studyDesign` for design characteristics and `classifier` for other groupings. Existing R4 instances need semantic classification before migration, but the old bucket was intentionally broad and keeping it would undermine the more computable split.
keyEvidence: R4 `ResearchStudy.category`: 0..* CodeableConcept, example binding, definition covers investigational/observational, blinding, randomization, safety/efficacy.
R4 mapping for `category` includes ClinicalTrials.gov Study Type, Primary Purpose, Interventional Model, Masking, Allocation, and Observational Study Model.
R6 `ResearchStudy.studyDesign`: 0..* CodeableConcept, preferred binding to `study-design`, same core definition and ClinicalTrials.gov/BRIDG mappings.
R6 `ResearchStudy.classifier`: additional grouping/categorization with an implementation note not to duplicate explicit semantics.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1/trial-use softens the burden of preserving a broad example-bound bucket, although the ClinicalTrials.gov-style classifications make the affected data practically relevant.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: `category` is absent in R6; migration may require human or terminology-specific classification between `studyDesign`, `classifier`, or other explicit elements.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept deprecated `category` alongside `studyDesign` and `classifier`, but that would preserve an ambiguous catch-all and create conflicting ways to express the same classification. The alternative is only partial and has real computability costs.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing Medium impact and Partial alternative judgment match the fresh assessment; the break is real but proportionate to the semantic split.

findings.title: focus changed from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference and left the summary set

newState.summary: R6 `focus` is 0..* CodeableReference, summary=false, with target profiles Medication, MedicinalProductDefinition, SubstanceDefinition, DeviceDefinition, and PlanDefinition.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `focus` is 0..* CodeableReference, summary=false, with target profiles Medication, MedicinalProductDefinition, SubstanceDefinition, DeviceDefinition, and PlanDefinition.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The JSON shape changed at the same path. R4 entries with `coding` directly under `focus` are invalid in R6; R6 reference values cannot be represented in R4 CodeableConcept without losing the resource identity.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow focus to be either a coded concept or a reference to concrete study focus resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain coded `focus` and add a reference companion instead of replacing it with CodeableReference.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is strong: the study focus may be either a code or a reference to a concrete Medication, DeviceDefinition, PlanDefinition, or similar resource, and CodeableReference is the idiomatic R6 datatype for that pattern. A less-breaking model could preserve old coded `focus` values, but it would duplicate the CodeableReference concept and complicate search, validation, and mapping. Those tradeoffs make the break probably justified, though not absolutely necessary.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A compatible base design could keep `focus` as repeating CodeableConcept and add a new `focusReference` or similarly named companion reference element. R4 coded focuses would remain valid and R6 could still carry resource references. The cost is a permanent split between coded and referenced focus data, possible duplicate representations of the same fact, and divergence from the standard CodeableReference representation used elsewhere in R6.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids the R4 code-shape break but creates parallel coded/reference representations and reconciliation burden.

evidence.detail: R4 type is CodeableConcept.
R6 type is CodeableReference with resource target profiles.
R6 sets isSummary=false.

examples.examplesMd: Coded R4 values can usually be wrapped; R6 references need policy.

findings.narrativeMd: `focus` is a high-risk retained-path change: code can still find the property name but the datatype and child shape are different.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 CodeableConcept focus values are old-valid/new-invalid until wrapped as `focus.concept`. R6 reference focuses are not R4-representable without extensions or lossy coding.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap old coded values in `focus.concept`. For R6 references, resolve to a safe coding only when semantically valid; otherwise preserve the reference in an extension for R4.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A choice/additive design could have preserved old JSON but would duplicate representations.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 changes `focus` from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference at the same path. R4 coded focus entries must be wrapped as `focus.concept`, while R6 can point to concrete Medication, DeviceDefinition, SubstanceDefinition, MedicinalProductDefinition, or PlanDefinition resources that R4 cannot natively represent. This is a meaningful codegen and validation break, but CodeableReference is a coherent R6 model for a value that can be either coded or referenced.
keyEvidence: R4 `ResearchStudy.focus`: 0..* CodeableConcept, summary=true, definition covers medications, foods, therapies, devices, and other concerns under study.
R6 `ResearchStudy.focus`: 0..* CodeableReference, target profiles include Medication, MedicinalProductDefinition, SubstanceDefinition, DeviceDefinition, and PlanDefinition.
R6 keeps the same focus definition but changes summary to false and requires CodeableReference child shape.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1/trial-use softens the stability claim, but the focus of a study can be clinically and commercially important, so the migration burden remains real.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 CodeableConcept JSON at `focus` is not the R6 CodeableReference shape; R6-to-R4 loss occurs for resource references.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A companion reference element could have preserved R4 coded `focus`, but it would split code and reference representations and diverge from the R6 CodeableReference pattern. The tradeoff is material enough that the break appears proportionate.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment are directionally correct; the fresh judgment treats the break as acceptable because the R6 datatype directly serves the modeling goal.

findings.title: location was renamed to region and its jurisdiction binding weakened

oldState.summary: R4 `location` is 0..* CodeableConcept, summary, extensibly bound to jurisdiction; it describes countries/regions where the study takes place.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `location` is 0..* CodeableConcept, summary, extensibly bound to jurisdiction; it describes countries/regions where the study takes place.

newState.summary: R6 `region` is 0..* CodeableConcept, summary, preferred-bound to terminology.hl7.org jurisdiction; it clarifies this is area/region rather than a precise location.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `region` is 0..* CodeableConcept, summary, preferred-bound to terminology.hl7.org jurisdiction; it clarifies this is area/region rather than a precise location.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The old path is invalid in R6, but the mapping to `region` is otherwise straightforward and normally lossless.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify region geography and avoid confusion with facility `site`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `location` with clearer region-focused wording or as a deprecated alias to `region`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying that the element represents a country, state, or region rather than a precise facility is reasonable. The R4 and R6 definitions otherwise align closely, so the hard path rename was not needed to meet the core modeling goal. Retaining the old name with improved wording would preserve R4 instances with modest long-term cost.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best alternative would keep `location` as the base wire element, update its short/definition to emphasize geographic region, and reserve `site` for facilities. If R6 strongly preferred the term `region`, it could add `region` while accepting deprecated `location`, though that duplicate-alias design would need consistency guidance. Either path is less disruptive than removing `location` outright.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The legacy name can be confused with facility `site`, but clearer definitions and guidance can manage that.

evidence.detail: R4 location is geographic region CodeableConcept.
R6 region has the same geographic concept.

examples.examplesMd: Do not map this to `site`; `site` is for facilities.

findings.narrativeMd: `location` became `region`; this is a high-confidence direct rename.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `location` fails R6 validation until renamed. R6 `region` can normally be mapped back to R4 `location`; only terminology binding strength/canonical differs.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename the path and keep `site` separate. Update terminology canonical handling for jurisdiction.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The path break could have been avoided by keeping `location` as a deprecated alias.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `location` became `region` with the same cardinality, datatype, summary flag, and essentially the same country/state/area meaning. The R6 name is clearer, but the hard path rename is not necessary to achieve that clarification. This is a narrow element-level break with straightforward migration, yet it is also a low-cost avoidable wire break.
keyEvidence: R4 `ResearchStudy.location`: 0..* CodeableConcept, summary=true, definition `country, state or other region where the study is taking place`.
R6 `ResearchStudy.region`: 0..* CodeableConcept, summary=true, definition `country, state or other area where the study is taking place rather than its precise geographic location or address`.
Both paths share BRIDG mapping `StudyProtocolVersion.participatingLocationCode`; R6 weakens the jurisdiction binding from extensible to preferred.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1/trial-use reduces the severity of this rename, but the field maps to study geography and the R6 goal could be met with definition text rather than a wire-name break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 instance using `location` has an unknown element in R6; reverse mapping from `region` is otherwise mostly lossless.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping `location` and clarifying its definition as geographic region would preserve old instances without duplicate data. If `region` were added as a preferred new name, the duplicate-alias option would need consistency rules, but keeping the old path is the lowest-cost base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing Medium impact and `Yes` alternative judgment are consistent with the fresh assessment, with FMM limiting the breadth rather than eliminating the avoidability concern.

findings.title: relatedArtifact was removed and replaced by relatesTo, citeAs, and result patterns

oldState.summary: R4 `relatedArtifact` is 0..* RelatedArtifact for citations, references, and related documents.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `relatedArtifact` is 0..* RelatedArtifact for citations, references, and related documents.

newState.summary: R6 removes `relatedArtifact`; `relatesTo` is a backbone with required `type` and `target[x]`, `citeAs` carries citation display, and `result` links generated results.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 removes `relatedArtifact`; `relatesTo` is a backbone with required `type` and `target[x]`, `citeAs` carries citation display, and `result` links generated results.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Overlap is clear but not one-to-one.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `relatedArtifact` is invalid in R6, and the replacement model is not datatype-compatible. Some RelatedArtifact uses map to relationship targets, some to citation text, and some to result links.

justification.inferredGoal: Make relationships, citation, and results more explicit.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Making relationships, citation display, and generated results more explicit is a reasonable R6 goal. A deprecated `relatedArtifact` would reduce wire breakage, but it would preserve a broad datatype beside the new purpose-specific model and would not solve the need to classify old RelatedArtifact payloads. The alternative is useful but incomplete, so the breaking remodel is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `relatedArtifact` for R4 compatibility and added the R6 `relatesTo`, `citeAs`, and `result` paths. That preserves old instances but creates duplicate same-resource ways to say that another artifact is documentation, citation, derived-from, or a result. Without strong consistency rules, deprecated `relatedArtifact` data could persist indefinitely and undermine the clearer R6 relationship model.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old instances but leaves overlapping relationship, citation, and result representations.

evidence.detail: R4 uses RelatedArtifact.
R6 uses a local relatesTo backbone.
R6 adds result references.

examples.examplesMd: Exact target choice depends on the R4 RelatedArtifact content.

findings.narrativeMd: The relationship model was split by use case. This is a codegen and transform break for systems that reused the `RelatedArtifact` datatype.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `relatedArtifact` is invalid in R6. R6 `relatesTo` targets and `result` references may not fit R4 RelatedArtifact without loss or extensions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Classify each old RelatedArtifact by type/payload. Map relationships to `relatesTo`, bibliographic display to `citeAs`, and result resources to `result`; preserve unhandled subfields in extensions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A deprecated old element would have been more compatible but kept overlapping ways to express relationships.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: A formal ConceptMap would improve mapping confidence.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `relatedArtifact` was removed in favor of more explicit R6 relationship, citation, and result patterns. R4 RelatedArtifact payloads are not mechanically equivalent to `relatesTo`, `citeAs`, and `result`, so migration may need classification and may preserve some content through extensions. Still, the R6 design addresses a real ambiguity in a broad datatype.
keyEvidence: R4 `ResearchStudy.relatedArtifact`: 0..* RelatedArtifact, definition `Citations, references and other related documents`, ClinicalTrials.gov mapping `Citations, Links, Available Study Data/Documents`.
R6 `ResearchStudy.relatesTo`: 0..* backbone with required `type` and required `target[x]` supporting uri, Attachment, canonical, Reference, or markdown.
R6 `ResearchStudy.citeAs`: markdown citation display; R6 `ResearchStudy.result`: references Composition, DiagnosticReport, DocumentReference, or Evidence.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1/trial-use softens compatibility expectations, but citations, protocols, links, and result documents are important in research/audit workflows.

freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Retaining deprecated `relatedArtifact` would preserve R4 wire format but leave overlapping ways to represent relationships and citations beside the clearer R6 paths. The alternative is partial and risks long-term inconsistency.

findings.title: enrollment was replaced by a singular recruitment backbone

oldState.summary: R4 `enrollment` is 0..* Reference(Group), summary, for criteria and quantity of subjects.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `enrollment` is 0..* Reference(Group), summary, for criteria and quantity of subjects.

newState.summary: R6 `recruitment` is 0..1 BackboneElement with targetNumber, actualNumber, eligibility, actualGroup, and description.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `recruitment` is 0..1 BackboneElement with targetNumber, actualNumber, eligibility, actualGroup, and description.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Definitions overlap, but role split is new.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `enrollment` is invalid in R6 and old repeated Group references may not reveal whether they are eligibility criteria, actual groups, or count surrogates.

justification.inferredGoal: Distinguish recruitment counts, eligibility groups, and actual enrolled groups.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `enrollment` while adding the `recruitment` backbone.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is reasonable because recruitment separates target counts, actual counts, eligibility groups, and actual enrolled groups. R4 `enrollment` was a repeated Group reference whose role was not computably distinguished. Keeping it would preserve old instances but would not provide a clean or complete base model for the new semantics, so the breaking design is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could retain `enrollment` as a deprecated repeating Reference(Group) and add `recruitment`. That covers R4 wire compatibility for common data. It is only partial because old references still need role classification, multiple old Groups may not fit the singular recruitment structure cleanly, and implementers would need rules to prevent `enrollment`, `recruitment.eligibility`, and `recruitment.actualGroup` from drifting apart.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old Group references but keeps ambiguous enrollment semantics beside explicit recruitment fields.

evidence.detail: R4 enrollment is 0..* Reference(Group).
R6 recruitment is a 0..1 backbone.
R6 eligibility is a Group reference with definitional/conceptual membership expectations.
R6 actualGroup is a Group reference with enumerated membership expectation.

examples.examplesMd: The example assumes roles that R4 did not enforce.

findings.narrativeMd: Recruitment/enrollment moved from a simple repeated reference to a richer singular backbone. That is a hard wire break and often a semantic migration problem.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `enrollment` fails R6 validation. R6 `actualGroup`, counts, and description have no native R4 ResearchStudy field. Multiple old enrollment references may not fit one R6 recruitment object without role classification.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Classify old Group references before mapping. Use `recruitment.eligibility` for definitional/conceptual criteria and `recruitment.actualGroup` for enumerated actual participants; preserve ambiguous or extra groups in extensions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: R6 could have kept the old field as a deprecated compatibility path, but that would perpetuate ambiguous enrollment semantics.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Group resource semantics are a follow-up dependency.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `enrollment` was a repeating Group reference that covered criteria and subject quantity. R6 replaces it with a singular `recruitment` backbone containing target/actual counts plus separate eligibility and actual enrolled Group references. The R6 model is clearer, but old repeated Group references may not say whether they are eligibility, actual enrolled participants, or cohort/group structure, so migration can require expert judgment for a central study-registry concept.
keyEvidence: R4 `ResearchStudy.enrollment`: 0..* Reference(Group), summary=true, definition includes criteria and quantity of subjects; comment says Group should generally not enumerate subjects.
R4 mapping for `enrollment` includes ClinicalTrials.gov Enrollment, Number of Groups/Cohorts, Groups, and Eligibility.
R6 `ResearchStudy.recruitment`: 0..1 backbone with targetNumber, actualNumber, eligibility, actualGroup, and description.
R6 `recruitment.eligibility` expects definitional/conceptual Group membership; `recruitment.actualGroup` expects enumerated Group membership.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1/trial-use softens pure stability expectations, but enrollment/eligibility data are central to clinical study exchange and plausibly regulatory/public-registry relevant.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `enrollment` is removed; migration from repeated Group references to one recruitment backbone may be lossy or require role classification.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could retain deprecated `enrollment` while adding `recruitment`, preserving old instances. The tradeoff is ambiguous duplicated semantics and synchronization rules, but the affected concept is central enough that a transitional base path merits renewed consideration.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing High impact and Partial alternative are right, but the fresh judgment is less comfortable with `probably justified` because the path is central and migration may be expert-dependent.

findings.title: sponsor, principalInvestigator, and contact were removed in favor of associatedParty role modeling

oldState.summary: R4 has separate `sponsor` 0..1 Reference(Organization), `principalInvestigator` 0..1 Reference(Practitioner|PractitionerRole), and `contact` 0..* ContactDetail.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain sponsor, principalInvestigator, and contact shortcuts while adding `associatedParty`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Generalizing study parties into a repeating role-coded backbone is a reasonable R6 goal, especially for sponsors, collaborators, investigators, funders, and contacts beyond the fixed R4 shortcuts. Deprecated shortcut elements could reduce breakage, but they would overlap with `associatedParty.role` and leave ContactDetail-vs-party representation questions unresolved. The material duplication and consistency risks make the breaking consolidation probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could keep `sponsor`, `principalInvestigator`, and `contact` as deprecated shortcuts and add `associatedParty` for richer role modeling. That would protect common R4 instances. The alternative is partial because the same sponsor or investigator could appear in two places, roles would need synchronization, and R4 `ContactDetail.telecom` content still does not map cleanly to the R6 party-reference shape without additional conventions.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves common R4 clients but creates duplicate party/contact representations and consistency rules.

evidence.detail: R4 sponsor is Reference(Organization).
R4 principalInvestigator is Reference(Practitioner|PractitionerRole).
R4 contact is ContactDetail.
R6 role is mandatory and includes sponsor/primary-investigator/contact-like role displays.

examples.examplesMd: The contact telecom requires a referenced party or extension for lossless preservation.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 consolidates parties and contacts into a role-based backbone. This improves expressivity but is a hard break for common R4 implementations.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 sponsor, principalInvestigator, and contact properties fail R6 validation. R6 can express many parties and roles that R4 cannot. Old ContactDetail telecoms have no obvious native associatedParty field in the supplied definition.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map sponsor to a sponsor/lead-sponsor role, principalInvestigator to primary-investigator, and contacts to general-contact or recruitment-contact only if details can be preserved through party references or extensions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Deprecated aliases would have protected common R4 data at the cost of duplicate role modeling.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Check ballot narrative for the inconsistent associatedParty comment before finalizing automated party transforms.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 separate sponsor, principalInvestigator, and contact paths were removed in favor of role-coded `associatedParty`. General party-role modeling is reasonable, but sponsor/legal responsibility, investigator responsibility, and contact details are common study registry concepts. R4 `ContactDetail` payloads also do not map cleanly to the R6 associatedParty shape, which has name, party reference, periods, and classifiers but no direct telecom/address fields.
keyEvidence: R4 `ResearchStudy.sponsor`: 0..1 Reference(Organization), definition `initiates the investigation and is legally responsible`, ClinicalTrials.gov mapping `Sponsor`.
R4 `ResearchStudy.principalInvestigator`: 0..1 Reference(Practitioner|PractitionerRole), ClinicalTrials.gov mapping `Principal Investigator`.
R4 `ResearchStudy.contact`: 0..* ContactDetail, ClinicalTrials.gov mapping includes central contacts, facility contacts, and investigators.
R6 has no `sponsor`, `principalInvestigator`, or `contact`; `associatedParty.role` is mandatory with preferred roles such as sponsor, primary-investigator, general-contact, and recruitment-contact.

R6 `associatedParty.party` is Reference(Practitioner|PractitionerRole|Organization), and `associatedParty.name` is string; no direct ContactDetail telecom/address equivalent appears in the element list.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1/trial-use softens the stability expectation, but party responsibility and contact data are central business/regulatory fields for studies.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: three R4 paths are removed; runtime/API/codegen break is likely for clients using sponsor/investigator/contact properties, and contact details may be lossy.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping deprecated sponsor, principalInvestigator, and contact shortcuts while adding `associatedParty` would preserve common R4 instances. The tradeoff is duplicate role representation and consistency rules, but the legal/contact semantics are important enough that this alternative remains plausible.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing High impact and Partial alternative are right, but the fresh review rates the design as needing reconsideration because common responsibility/contact data are not cleanly preserved.

findings.title: reasonStopped was renamed to whyStopped

oldState.summary: R4 `reasonStopped` is 0..1 CodeableConcept, summary, example-bound to research-study-reason-stopped.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `reasonStopped` is 0..1 CodeableConcept, summary, example-bound to research-study-reason-stopped.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The old path is invalid in R6, but the datatype, cardinality, summary flag, and definition are stable, making migration a direct rename in most cases.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `reasonStopped` or accept it as a deprecated alias for `whyStopped`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 element has the same cardinality, datatype, summary flag, and definition family as R4. The apparent goal is only wording cleanup. Because the old path could have been retained with little cost, this hard serialization break is probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The base model could simply have kept `reasonStopped` and updated terminology canonical references. If the shorter name was important, R6 could add `whyStopped` while accepting deprecated `reasonStopped`; the duplicate risk is low because the concept is singular and directly equivalent.

evidence.detail: R4 has reasonStopped with premature-termination definition.
R6 has whyStopped with the same definition.

findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename the element and update terminology canonical references in local profiles/validators.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This appears avoidable because the semantics did not change.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `reasonStopped` was renamed to `whyStopped` while preserving cardinality, datatype, summary flag, definition, example binding family, and mappings. The migration is straightforward, but the break appears to buy only wording cleanup for a safety/regulatory-relevant concept: why a study ended prematurely.

R6 `ResearchStudy.whyStopped`: 0..1 CodeableConcept, summary=true, same definition and same ClinicalTrials.gov/BRIDG mappings.
The binding family remains `research-study-reason-stopped`, with the value set canonical moved to terminology.hl7.org.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1/trial-use softens the practical severity and migration is direct, but premature stop reasons can be safety/audit relevant and the rename has little apparent modeling benefit.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `reasonStopped` is absent in R6; R6 `whyStopped` maps back directly apart from the path and terminology canonical.

findings.title: arm was replaced by comparisonGroup and expanded

oldState.summary: R4 `arm` is 0..* BackboneElement with required `arm.name`, optional `arm.type`, and optional string `arm.description`.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `arm` is 0..* BackboneElement with required `arm.name`, optional `arm.type`, and optional string `arm.description`.

newState.summary: R6 `comparisonGroup` is 0..* BackboneElement with alias `arm`, optional `name`, markdown `description`, and added targetNumber, actualNumber, eligibility, and observedGroup.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `comparisonGroup` is 0..* BackboneElement with alias `arm`, optional `name`, markdown `description`, and added targetNumber, actualNumber, eligibility, and observedGroup.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: R6 alias and mappings identify this as the replacement.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `arm` is invalid in R6. The likely replacement has changed child requirements and added fields that cannot be represented in R4 arm.

justification.inferredGoal: Use terminology that applies beyond clinical trial arms and capture comparison-group details.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `arm` as the wire element, broaden its definition, add comparison-group children, and retain old children.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Broadening the concept beyond clinical-trial arms and adding comparison-group details is reasonable. But the R6 definition already aliases `comparisonGroup` as `arm`, and the compatibility-preserving design does not require duplicate top-level fields: R6 could have kept `arm`, broadened its definition, and added the new optional children. Under the calibration rule that living with a nonoptimal R4 name can be legitimate, the hard path rename is probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could keep `ResearchStudy.arm` as `0..*`, revise its definition to mean comparison group across study types, add `targetNumber`, `actualNumber`, `eligibility`, and `observedGroup`, make `name` optional if desired, and retain or deprecate `arm.type`. Old R4 arm instances would still validate while R6 gained the richer model. The tradeoff is that non-clinical studies would continue to see the historical word `arm`, but aliases, definitions, and profile guidance are a moderate cost compared with a hard rename.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The word `arm` is less general, but aliases and definitions could handle that without duplicate top-level paths.

evidence.detail: R4 arm is 0..* BackboneElement with required name.
R6 comparisonGroup has alias `arm` and added children.

examples.examplesMd: Old `arm.type` has no direct R6 comparisonGroup child.

findings.narrativeMd: `arm` became `comparisonGroup`; this is clear from alias and mappings, but child content also changed.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `arm` fails R6 validation. R6 comparisonGroup without a name is valid but cannot satisfy R4 `arm.name`; R6 count/group fields are not R4-representable.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `arm` to `comparisonGroup`. Move `name` and `description`; review old `arm.type` for mapping to studyDesign/classifier/extension. Preserve new R6 count/group fields in R4 extensions if needed.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The broader name and richer model are plausible, but a deprecated alias would have avoided the hard break.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `arm` became R6 `comparisonGroup`, with alias `arm` and a broadened definition that applies beyond clinical trial arms. R6 also changes child semantics by making `name` optional, changing `description` to markdown, removing `type`, and adding count/group details. The broader model is reasonable, but the top-level rename looks avoidable because R6 could have kept `arm` as the wire element while broadening its definition and adding optional children.
keyEvidence: R4 `ResearchStudy.arm`: 0..* backbone, ClinicalTrials.gov mapping `Arms`, BRIDG mapping `Arm`.
R4 `arm.name`: required string; `arm.type`: optional CodeableConcept; `arm.description`: optional string.
R6 `ResearchStudy.comparisonGroup`: 0..* backbone with alias `arm`, comment that clinical trials call this ARM but other trials do not.
R6 `comparisonGroup.name`: optional; `description`: markdown; added targetNumber, actualNumber, eligibility, and observedGroup.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1/trial-use softens the general stability claim, but arms/comparison groups are central in clinical trial exchange and ClinicalTrials.gov-style mappings.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `arm` is absent in R6; R6-to-R4 loss exists for nameless comparison groups, counts, eligibility, observedGroup, and the removed old `arm.type` mapping.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could retain `ResearchStudy.arm`, broaden the definition to comparison groups, keep or deprecate `arm.type`, and add the new optional children. The main tradeoff is the less-general historical name, but R6 already carries `arm` as an alias and explanatory comment.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing High impact and `Yes` alternative judgment are supported; the rename is a central avoidable wire break even under low FMM.

findings.title: site now allows Organization and ResearchStudy references in addition to Location

impact.impactRationaleMd: All R4 Location references remain valid in R6, so this is not a forward hard break. R6 instances using Organization or ResearchStudy references at `site` are not valid R4 `site` values.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; this is a reference-target widening that preserves R4 Location references.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: This finding is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue because every R4 `site` Reference(Location) remains valid under the wider R6 target list. The broader targets may need clearer narrative and down-conversion policy, but there is no old-valid/new-invalid break to avoid.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because the change only widens allowed targets, a backward-compatible alternative is not applicable. Separate elements for organization-based sites or study-site groupings might have clarified semantics, but that would be an alternate R6 model rather than a less-breaking way to preserve R4 instances. R6-to-R4 conversion still needs a policy for Organization and ResearchStudy references.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is needed; R6-to-R4 conversion must handle Organization and ResearchStudy targets.

evidence.detail: R4 target profile is Location only.
R6 target profiles are Location, ResearchStudy, and Organization.

examples.examplesMd: This R6 site is not a valid R4 site target.

findings.narrativeMd: `site` kept its path but widened reference targets. This mainly affects down-conversion and R4-era code that assumes every site resolves to Location.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4 instance is invalidated by this change alone. R6 Organization or ResearchStudy site references cannot be represented in R4 without conversion to Location, extension, or loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, leave Location site references unchanged. For R6-to-R4, check target type and define policy for Organization/ResearchStudy references.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `site` kept the same path, cardinality, summary flag, and Location target while adding Organization and ResearchStudy as additional allowable targets. This does not invalidate R4 instances. The concern is only that R6 instances using the new target types need an R4 down-conversion policy.

R6 `ResearchStudy.site`: 0..* Reference(Location|ResearchStudy|Organization), same short/definition and mappings.

freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed for R4 compatibility. Separate elements might clarify semantics, but they would not be less breaking than simply widening the target list.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly says there is no forward hard break and no applicable less-breaking alternative, but its Medium overall impact overstates this as a fresh R4-to-R6 compatibility concern.

findings.title: R6 adds substantial optional ResearchStudy content with no native R4 representation

affectedLocation.newPath: ResearchStudy.url / version / name / label / citeAs / date / descriptionSummary / progressStatus / objective.outcomeMeasure / result
affectedLocation.newElementId: ResearchStudy.url / version / name / label / citeAs / date / descriptionSummary / progressStatus / objective.outcomeMeasure / result

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 lacks these local ResearchStudy elements; equivalent information would require extensions, related resources, or narrative conventions.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional canonical-like metadata, labels/citation, progress status, objective descriptions/outcome measures, and result links.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional canonical-like metadata, labels/citation, progress status, objective descriptions/outcome measures, and result links.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional additions do not invalidate old R4 instances, but R6 instances using them carry data that base R4 ResearchStudy cannot serialize natively.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent richer registry, publication, progress, outcome, and result metadata.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; optional R6 additions do not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The added R6 metadata, progress, outcome, and result elements address real modeling gaps and are optional, so they preserve R4-to-R6 compatibility for existing instances. The compatibility problem is R6-to-R4 data loss, not an avoidable breaking R6 base design.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base R6 alternative is applicable because adding optional elements is already the compatibility-preserving way to extend the model. R4 extensions, companion resources, or conversion guidance can mitigate down-conversion loss, but those are backport strategies and should not be counted as a `Yes` alternative to a breaking R6 design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 backporting needs extensions or companion resources, but that is down-conversion rather than a base R6 alternative.

evidence.detail: R6 adds progressStatus with state, actual, and period.
R6 adds outcomeMeasure with endpoint and analysis-related children.
R6 adds result references.

examples.examplesMd: Base R4 has no local fields for these R6 additions.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 introduces many optional local fields. They are not R4-to-R6 breaking, but they are important for round-trip and R4-client interoperability.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 validators reject these R6-only paths. Dropping progressStatus, outcomeMeasure, or result links can lose clinically or scientifically meaningful information.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define cross-version extensions or companion-resource conventions for R4 output. Add tests to prevent silent loss of progress status, outcome measures, and result references.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because these are optional forward additions, the main compatibility need is explicit R4 extension guidance rather than changing R6.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Highest data-loss risk is in progressStatus, objective.outcomeMeasure, and result.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The finding is about optional R6 additions: canonical-like metadata, labels/citation, progress status, richer objective/outcome-measure structure, and result links. These do not break R4 instances moving to R6; the compatibility issue is R6-to-R4 loss when an R6 sender uses the new data. Because optional additions are the normal less-breaking way to extend a trial-use resource, the design appears proportionate even though conversion guidance is important.
keyEvidence: R6 adds optional top-level `url`, `version`, `name`, `label`, `citeAs`, `date`, `descriptionSummary`, `progressStatus`, and `result`; R4 has none of these local ResearchStudy paths.
R6 `progressStatus.state` is required within each progressStatus entry and binds to research-study-status; `actual` and `period` add timing semantics.
R6 `objective.description` and `objective.outcomeMeasure` add endpoint, population, intervention, comparator, summary measure, analysis plan, and event-handling detail absent from R4 objective.
R6 `result` references Composition, DiagnosticReport, DocumentReference, or Evidence and explicitly may link to ClinicalTrials.gov-style results.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 1/trial-use makes optional forward additions especially acceptable, but study progress, outcomes, and results can be scientifically and regulatory relevant when down-converting.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6-only optional data cannot be serialized natively in base R4 ResearchStudy; no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break is present.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is applicable because optional additions are already the compatibility-preserving design. R4 extensions or companion-resource conventions are mitigation for down-conversion, not a less-breaking R6 base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing Medium R6-to-R4 impact and Not applicable alternative judgment are reasonable, with the fresh review emphasizing that this is not a forward hard break.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6-to-R4 conversion must decide whether to merge or extend summary text.
